policy_posture.description: This vocabulary classifies observed tool-use patterns for audit and telemetry only. Domain tools, dispatch/readiness tools, runtime refusal layers, and WK-1438 routing metadata remain the authority for behavior.

routing_intent_contract.reason: packages/wiki-core/data/tool-routing-intents.v1.json is empty in this slice; this policy uses only coarse replacement-family references and does not define routing-intent identifiers.

severity_levels.description: Observed pattern is useful for trend analysis and does not imply immediate remediation.
Observed pattern is inefficient or weakly sequenced, but usually recoverable without changing durable state.
Observed pattern can waste substantial context, skip a documented prerequisite, or obscure audit evidence.
Observed pattern can bypass an authority-bearing validation step or create high-risk coordination ambiguity.

recoverability_levels.description: A follow-up call can usually return the workflow to the expected sequence.
A coordinator or operator should inspect the run before treating the workflow as complete.
The audit vocabulary can identify the pattern, but it cannot repair or authorize a replacement action.

replacement_families.description: Use a compact status, frontier, or next-action lens before search or record sampling for broad state questions.
Use a compact read of resources selected by a prior lens, status, search, or router result before detailed/full expansion.
Use a bounded lens, filtered summary, or selected-resource view instead of broad sampling without a stated selection lens.
Run the structured dispatch-readiness validation path before role dispatch.
replacement_families.exact_call_authority: dispatch readiness tooling and WK-1438 router output when available

replacement_families.description: Follow the required next_action or allowed-next-call signal returned by the previous authoritative tool response.
Request compact or summarized output before high-output, verbose, full, or bulk views unless prior selected context requires detail.

misuse_codes.title: Search used for status aggregation
misuse_codes.summary: A search/discovery call was used as the first or primary step for initiative status, frontier state, next action, or dispatch-state aggregation.

misuse_codes.title: Full read without selected resource
misuse_codes.summary: A full or detailed resource read was requested before a compact/lens/search/router result selected the resource or established the need for detail.

misuse_codes.title: Bulk sampling without lens
misuse_codes.summary: Multiple records, files, runs, or pages were sampled to infer aggregate state without first using a compact lens, status, or filtered summary.

misuse_codes.title: Dispatch without readiness validation
misuse_codes.summary: A worker, reviewer, redteam, or role-session dispatch was attempted before the structured dispatch-readiness validation path established the unit is dispatchable.

misuse_codes.title: Ignored required next action
misuse_codes.summary: A tool response supplied a required next_action, selected-resource follow-up, or allowed-next-call boundary, but the subsequent observed call did not follow it.

misuse_codes.title: High-output option without compact first
misuse_codes.summary: A verbose, full, high-output, bulk, or unbounded response mode was requested before a compact response or selected-resource prerequisite justified the larger output.
